note: Shows n-gram decontamination is defeated by paraphrase, and finds 8 to 18 percent HumanEval overlap in common pretraining sets.
title: Rethinking Benchmark and Contamination for Language Models with Rephrased Samples
explain_beginner: Researchers discovered that popular methods for cleaning training data before building AI language models are not working well enough. When test questions are slightly reworded or translated, current cleaning techniques miss them completely. This means models can accidentally memorize test data and appear smarter than they actually are. The team found that 8 to 18 percent of common test sets were hidden in training data. They created a better cleaning method and released it publicly to help the community build more trustworthy AI systems.
explain_business: Organizations relying on benchmark scores to evaluate language model capabilities may be making decisions based on inflated performance metrics due to hidden training data overlap. This work reveals that current quality assurance practices are insufficient, creating risks in model selection and deployment decisions. The findings suggest investing in stronger decontamination processes and developing new evaluation methods. Companies should consider using the authors' publicly available decontamination tool and prioritize developing fresh benchmarks to obtain accurate performance assessments for competitive and technical decision-making.
explain_practitioner: This work demonstrates that n-gram based decontamination fails against paraphrased and translated benchmark samples. The authors developed an LLM-based decontamination approach and applied it to RedPajama-Data-1T and StarCoder-Data, discovering 8-18 percent HumanEval overlap in pre-training sets. Experiments on MMLU, GSK8k, and HumanEval show that without removing these variations, a 13B model achieves GPT-4 level performance through overfitting rather than capability gains. Notably, contamination also appears in synthetic datasets from GPT-3.5 and GPT-4, indicating unintentional data leakage during generation.
